transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Amaris Head of ML), Maya Li (Amaris Platform Eng), Evan Brooks (Amaris CTO)

Summary: quick discovery to understand Amaris's model selection needs across Hosted / Dedicated / Private options. Main topics: context length, multilingual support, tool-calling / function calls, latency vs cost, security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS), and pilot/benchmark next steps.

Topics: model family preferences, current stack (self-hosted + cloud), data residency, expected qps and latency SLOs, regen/rerank needs, tool-calling for internal apps.

-- Transcript --
00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan Miles from Redwood, AE. Uh Priya our solutions engineer is here as well. You all good on time?
00:12 Carlos: Yeah thanks, perfect. Appreciate it. I'm Carlos, I lead ML at Amaris.
00:16 Evan: Evan here, CTO. We'll mostly listen in for the high level, Maya will get into the infra details.
00:25 Priya: Great. Quick agenda, 1) understand current workloads and constraints, 2) talk model selection — context length, multilingual, tool-calling, 3) deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private), 4) next steps / pilot. Sound good?
00:37 Carlos: Yep. To start, quick context. We run a chat assistant for our enterprise clients and a code-assist feature for internal devs. Currently self-hosting mixed open models on GCP, but ops overhead is huge. Latency varies a lot. We're evaluating Redwood to either migrate to hosted for speed of launch or dedicate capacity for predictability; considering private for certain regulated customers.
00:58 Jordan: Good, helps. Two immediate model questions — one is context length. What are your typical prompt + convo sizes?
01:07 Maya: For the client-facing assistant, history can go up to 40k tokens in the largest cases, but the median is around 8k. For code assist, sometimes 32k, especially on big repos.
01:21 Priya: Got it. So support for long context is a big factor. We have models that support 8k, 32k, and some 64k variants — and we also offer KV cache/prefix cache strategies to reduce token cost and improve latency.
01:34 Carlos: When you say KV cache, does that work across sessions or just single request?
01:39 Priya: It's per-inference session, but we do prefix caching — so repeating system prompts or static context can be cached. For cross-session long-term memory you'd integrate with your store and Redwood can fetch on-demand; we can show a pattern in the POC.
01:52 Evan: Another question — multilingual. We need high quality in English, Spanish, Portuguese, and occasional French. Some docs are in Japanese too. How do the open models compare?
02:04 Priya: Good question. Broadly: Llama-family variants are strong in English and some European languages, Mistral and Mosaic-small variants vary, and there are some models specifically trained with better multilingual corpora. We typically recommend evaluating 2-3 model families on your data. Redwood's model catalog tags models by multilingual performance and we can run evals on your own prompts.
02:28 Carlos: Any gotchas with tokenizer differences for languages — like Japanese handling?
02:33 Priya: Tokenization can change cost and effective context. Some models use byte-level BPE which helps with Japanese. We'll include tokenizer sizes in the evaluation spreadsheet.
02:41 Jordan: Let's talk tool-calling / function calling — we need the model to call our internal tools (search, ticket create, run query). Does Redwood support that?
02:51 Priya: Yes — streaming with structured tool calls is supported. We support function-like tool invocation pattern, with safe fallbacks. In Dedicated/Private you can run the function-call handler inside your VPC so the data never leaves. There are small caveats with large-token tool outputs — streaming helps.
03:12 Maya: So for private deployments, what parts are managed vs customer-managed? Network and keys?
03:18 Jordan: For Private we provide a control plane but customer can manage networking and KMS/HSM. You can choose on-prem connectors or VPC peering depending on your compliance needs.
03:27 Evan: SOC2 / ISO — do you have certs and audit logs?
03:30 Jordan: Yes, hosted and dedicated customers can reference our SOC2 and ISO docs. For Private we provide hooks to your audit logging and we can generate x-forwarded logs; we'll share how audit events map to our platform.
03:41 Carlos: Latency vs cost — what does Redwood recommend for chat vs code-assist? Code-assist needs sub-200ms token latency ideally. Chat is more tolerant.
03:49 Priya: Right — for code-assist we usually recommend a lower-latency model variant on Dedicated capacity with optimized kernels and minimal batching. Also quantized models with mixed precision can help. For chat where throughput matters, batching and caching reduce cost. We can show concrete per-token cost tradeoffs in the pricing sheet.
04:07 Maya: Do you do kernel selection automatically? Any tuning needed for our specific hardware?
04:12 Priya: The runtime does kernel selection based on model arch and sequence length distribution. For Dedicated we tune batch sizes and kernel paddings during onboarding; we can iterate during the POC.
04:22 Carlos: How about fallback policies? If Dedicated capacity maxes out, can requests go to hosted as a fallback?
04:28 Jordan: Yes, smart routing can failover to compatible variants and different tiers/regions. You set policies — e.g., cost-first, latency-first, or safety-first.
04:36 Evan: On the model side, we want to avoid hallucinations for sensitive responses and allow reranking. Is reranking supported?
04:42 Priya: We support n-best outputs and reranking flows; Redwood Optimize can suggest model/quantization profiles and run quality evaluations tied to prompt sets. We'll run regression tests as part of pilot.
04:54 Carlos: Good. For the POC, we'd like to compare 1) a hosted quick test for latency and output quality, 2) Dedicated reserved capacity for code-assist peak qps, and 3) Private for our regulated clients. What's a reasonable scope?
05:07 Jordan: Conservative scope: 2-3 models, your representative prompt set (10-50 prompts per workflow), a 1-hour load/latency run + quality eval. We'll provide a benchmark template.
05:18 Maya: About traffic profile — we have spikes up to 120 rps for chat and sustained 30 rps for code-assist during working hours.
05:25 Priya: Noted. That helps size Dedicated. We'll recommend GPU types and batch configs.

-- Mid-call clarifications, slight transcript noise --
18:02 Carlos: sorry jumped — are you able to run canned re-ranking pipelines on your side or do we need to host them?
18:09 Priya: You can host reranker as a Redwood function or keep it in your infra and call via tool-calls. Both patterns are common.

-- security / compliance deep dive snippet --
29:30 Evan: For Private we need to ensure KMS integration with our HSM provider, and SSO via SAML. Any known blockers?
29:37 Jordan: We integrate with common KMS providers and support customer-managed HSM via connectors. SAML SSO is supported and RBAC is plumbed through the console. We'll share our integration notes.
29:49 Maya: Data residency — some EU clients can't have data outside EU. Is Private the only path?
29:54 Jordan: For strict residency yes, Private or Dedicated in EU region; hosted can be regionally isolated but for absolute control Private is recommended.

-- Closing 10 minutes: recap and next steps --
45:10 Jordan: Quick recap — 1) we'll send pricing and hosted vs dedicated comparison, 2) Priya will prepare pilot runbook and onboarding checklist, 3) you (Maya) will send sample prompts and 2 weeks of traffic profile. We also agreed to run a 1-hour latency/cost benchmark.
45:35 Carlos: That sounds right. Timeline wise we want to start pilot early Dec.
45:40 Jordan: We'll aim for POC kickoff week of Dec 6. Action items we'll email after.
45:46 Evan: For the pilot, can you include the tokenizer and breaking-down token estimates? That mattered with our Japanese workloads.
45:52 Priya: Absolutely. We'll include tokenizer delta and expected token counts per prompt.
46:00 Jordan: Anything else before we wrap?
46:03 Maya: One ask — can you include a quick reference: which models support function-calling streaming vs which ones have chunked outputs?
46:10 Priya: Yep, we'll add a model capability matrix in the deck.
46:15 Jordan: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with docs and the pricing sheet.
46:20 Carlos: Thanks. Appreciate it.

-- End of call --
